title: 33.4: A Wideband Bidirectional Calibration-Free Frequency/Switching-Staggering 360° D-Band Phase Shifter with Frequency-Invariant Codes Achieving lt; 2.38°/0.63dB RMS-Errors Over 24% Bandwidth
problem: D-band (110-170GHz) phased arrays for 6G require compact, bidirectional phase shifters (PSs) with 360° range, fine resolution (~4-6b), low phase/gain error, frequency-independent codes, and low power—existing designs trade off area, accuracy, or bandwidth.
motivation: Beyond-5G and 6G wireless demand large phased arrays with tight λ/2×λ/2 element spacing (1mm×1mm at 150GHz); accurate, calibration-free beamforming requires PSs without gain/phase variation across frequency and states.
method: The device shifts the phase (timing) of radio signals across the D-band (110-170 GHz range for 6G). Using a frequency/switching-staggering technique (adjusting when different parts activate based on the signal frequency), the phase shifts work equally well across a 24% range of frequencies without needing manual calibration. It achieves less than 2.38° phase error and less than 0.63dB gain error (signal strength error), and the same device handles both transmit and receive signals.
key_novelty: The frequency/switching-staggering technique (adjusting when different parts activate based on the signal frequency) enables phase adjustment codes that work across a 24% bandwidth without manual tuning, achieving phase errors below 2.38° and gain errors below 0.63dB.
contributions: Calibration-free D-band phase shifter with frequency-invariant codes
Bidirectional TX/RX sharing for compact phased arrays
<2.38° RMS phase error and <0.63dB RMS gain error over 24% bandwidth
360° phase range with ~6b resolution in compact form factor
